task.title: Compare long numeric prerelease identifiers without int conversion (python-semver issue #487)
task.statement: python-semver (src/semver, BSD-3) is a semantic-versioning library whose central class is semver.version.Version (also exported as semver.Version). Bug report (upstream issue #487): Version.is_valid("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000) is True, but Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000).compare(...) raises ValueError, because Version._nat_cmp in src/semver/version.py converts every all-digit prerelease identifier with int() and CPython refuses int conversion of strings longer than 4300 digits. Fix the prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so that it never converts a long ASCII numeric identifier to an int, while keeping the existing ordering rules exactly. Required semantics of the prerelease comparison: identifiers are the dot-separated parts of the prerelease string (an empty or None prerelease has one empty identifier); an identifier consisting only of ASCII digits is numeric and compares by its decimal value, computed without int(): strip leading zeros (an all-zero identifier becomes "0"), compare by length first and then lexicographically; a numeric identifier is lower than any non-numeric identifier; two non-numeric identifiers compare as plain strings; when every identifier of the shorter list is equal, the longer list is higher. Preserve the constructor's legacy behaviour: Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=...) accepts identifiers with leading zeros and identifiers written with non-ASCII decimal digits (str.isdigit() is true), and such non-ASCII digit identifiers keep comparing by their int() value, so "١٢" compares equal to "12" and "１２" is lower than "13"; an identifier for which str.isdigit() is true but int() fails (for example "²") must still make compare() raise ValueError, eagerly, even when an earlier identifier would already decide the order, but only when the core versions are equal: a difference in major, minor or patch is decided before the prerelease is examined, so Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True. Keep everything else unchanged: Version.parse keeps rejecting non-canonical prereleases such as "01", "01.2", "١٢" and "１２" with ValueError; build metadata is ignored in comparisons; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same core version without one; the prerelease attribute is stored as given. Do not change parsing, the optional native parser, tests, docs or packaging files, and keep the whole existing pytest suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: With v = "0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000: Version.is_valid(v) is True; Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0; compare(v, "0.0.0-2") == 1 and compare("0.0.0-2", v) == -1 (no ValueError).

Ordering of long numeric prereleases with Version.parse("0.0.0-" + x): "9" * 4999 < "1" + "0" * 4999; "1" + "0" * 4998 + "1" < "1" + "0" * 4998 + "2"; "1" * 5000 < "alpha"; "alpha." + "1" * 5000 < "alpha." + "1" * 5000 + ".1". For each pair low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1 and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
Build metadata is ignored and release order is preserved: with version = Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000), version == version.replace(build="other") and version < Version(0, 0, 0).

Constructor prereleases compare with the legacy rules, as Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)): ("0001", "1") -> 0; ("000", "0") -> 0; ("02", "10") -> -1; ("01.2", "1.2") -> 0; ("2a", "10a") -> 1; ("01a", "1a") -> -1; ("-1", "0") -> 1; ("", None) -> 0; ("١٢", "12") -> 0; ("１２", "13") -> -1; ("1٢", "12") -> 0; ("٠٠١", "1") -> 0; the reverse comparison gives the negated result and both .prerelease attributes are stored as given.
Version.parse("0.0.0-" + p) raises ValueError for p in ("01", "01.2", "١٢", "１２").
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)) raises ValueError for (left, right) in (("²", "2"), ("a.²", "b.0"), ("a.0", "b.²")).
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True (the core comparison decides before the prerelease is examined).
The existing pytest suite in tests/ passes unchanged.

spec.restated_task: Fix prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so ASCII numeric identifiers of arbitrary length compare by normalized decimal strings without integer conversion, while preserving existing version precedence, constructor permissiveness, Unicode-digit integer semantics, eager conversion errors, parsing restrictions, and public APIs. Limit implementation changes to this file's prerelease comparison logic and keep the existing pytest suite unchanged and passing.

interface_contract.name: semver.version.Version (also semver.Version and VersionInfo)
interface_contract.signature: Version(major: SupportsInt, minor: SupportsInt = 0, patch: SupportsInt = 0, prerelease: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None, build: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None)
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve construction unchanged. Core parts are converted to integers. Prerelease and build are stored as None or str(argument); string prereleases retain their exact spelling, including leading zeros, Unicode digits, and empty strings. Constructor acceptance does not imply parser acceptance.
error_cases: ValueError: a converted core component is negative.
TypeError or ValueError: existing core integer conversion fails. Preserve existing constructor errors.

interface_contract.name: Version._nat_cmp
interface_contract.behavior: Retain this existing internal comparison entry point. Split each value on dots, treating None and empty string as one empty identifier. A nonempty identifier containing only ASCII digits is numeric: strip leading ASCII zeros, represent an all-zero identifier as '0', then compare numeric values by normalized length and lexicographic order without int conversion. As a compatibility exception, an identifier containing non-ASCII characters whose str.isdigit() is true retains int(identifier) semantics and is numeric if conversion succeeds, including mixed ASCII/Unicode digits. Such numeric values compare by decimal value against ASCII numeric values as well. Other identifiers, including empty identifiers, are non-numeric and compare using ordinary Python string ordering. Numeric identifiers precede non-numeric identifiers. Compare identifiers left to right; after an equal shared prefix, the list with more identifiers is greater. Return exactly -1, 0, or 1. Validate all legacy Unicode-digit conversions in both lists before returning an ordering result; do not mutate inputs.
error_cases: ValueError: any non-ASCII-containing identifier has str.isdigit() true but int(identifier) fails, even if an earlier identifier or the list lengths would determine the result. Preserve interpreter integer-conversion limits for this legacy branch.
ASCII numeric identifiers must not raise integer-conversion-limit errors, regardless of their length or leading-zero count.

interface_contract.name: Version.compare
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve existing operand coercion for Version, str, bytes, dict, tuple, and list. Return exactly -1, 0, or 1. Compare major, minor, and patch first; a core difference returns before examining prereleases. For equal cores, evaluate prerelease comparison, including eager errors, before applying release precedence. None and empty prereleases compare equal and represent absence for release precedence; a nonempty prerelease is lower than absence. Build metadata is ignored.
error_cases: TypeError: unsupported operand type, preserving existing behavior.
TypeError or ValueError: existing operand parsing or construction fails.
ValueError: equal-core operands contain a legacy digit identifier whose int conversion fails, including when the other operand has no prerelease.

interface_contract.name: Version comparison operators
interface_contract.signature: __eq__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __ne__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __lt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __le__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __gt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; __ge__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool
interface_contract.behavior: Continue deriving results from compare, so equality, ordering, and sorting support long ASCII numeric prereleases. Preserve the existing decorator's NotImplemented behavior for unsupported operands and collections that cannot construct a version.
error_cases: ValueError: propagate prerelease comparison errors for successfully constructed equal-core operands.
Preserve existing parsing errors and Python operator behavior following NotImplemented.

interface_contract.name: Version.parse
interface_contract.signature: @classmethod parse(cls: Type[T], version: String, optional_minor_and_patch: bool = False) -> T
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged. Accept canonical prereleases containing arbitrarily long ASCII numeric identifiers, retaining their text. Continue strict prerelease validation and existing optional-minor/patch and optional-native-backend behavior.
error_cases: ValueError: invalid SemVer input, including prereleases '01', '01.2', '١٢', and '１２'.
TypeError: unsupported input type. Preserve existing byte decoding and other parsing errors.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_valid
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged: return True when parse succeeds and False when parse raises ValueError. A canonical 5000-digit ASCII numeric prerelease is valid.
error_cases: Errors other than ValueError retain their existing propagation behavior.

interface_contract.name: semver.compare
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing deprecated wrapper and warning behavior. Its delegation to Version.parse(ver1).compare(ver2) must inherit the fixed long-identifier comparison.
error_cases: Preserve parsing and comparison exceptions from the delegated operations.

interface_contract.name: Version.replace
interface_contract.behavior: Remain unchanged: return a new instance with requested parts replaced. Replacing only build metadata must preserve comparison equality, including for long numeric prereleases.
error_cases: TypeError: unknown replacement keys, preserving existing behavior.
Preserve other errors from constructing the replacement instance.

acceptance_criteria: 1. With v = '0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000, Version.is_valid(v) is True, Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0, semver.compare(v, '0.0.0-2') == 1, and semver.compare('0.0.0-2', v) == -1, without ValueError.

2. For each prerelease pair (low, high): ('9' * 4999, '1' + '0' * 4999), ('1' + '0' * 4998 + '1', '1' + '0' * 4998 + '2'), ('1' * 5000, 'alpha'), and ('alpha.' + '1' * 5000, 'alpha.' + '1' * 5000 + '.1'), parse each with core 0.0.0 and verify low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1, and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
3. For version = Version.parse('0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000), version == version.replace(build='other') and version < Version(0, 0, 0). Reverse comparisons have the corresponding opposite ordering.

4. Using equal-core directly constructed versions, verify these (left, right, result) cases: ('0001', '1', 0), ('000', '0', 0), ('02', '10', -1), ('01.2', '1.2', 0), ('2a', '10a', 1), ('01a', '1a', -1), ('-1', '0', 1), ('', None, 0), ('١٢', '12', 0), ('１２', '13', -1), ('1٢', '12', 0), and ('٠٠١', '1', 0). Reverse comparisons return the negated result, and each prerelease attribute remains exactly as supplied.

5. Directly constructed prereleases '0' * 5000 and '0' compare equal; '0' * 5000 + '12' compares equal to both '12' and '١٢'; '1' * 5000 compares greater than '１２'. No ASCII numeric identifier is converted to an integer, including when compared with a legacy Unicode numeric identifier.

6. Identifier boundaries and empty parts retain their meaning: Version._nat_cmp('', None) == 0, Version._nat_cmp('a', 'a.') == -1, Version._nat_cmp('a..b', 'a..c') == -1, and Version._nat_cmp('0', '') == -1. At the public version level, prerelease '0' remains lower than an absent prerelease.
7. Version.parse('0.0.0-' + p) raises ValueError for each p in ('01', '01.2', '١٢', '１２'); Version.is_valid returns False for the same strings.

8. Equal-core directly constructed versions raise ValueError for prerelease pairs ('²', '2'), ('a.²', 'b.0'), and ('a.0', 'b.²'), in both operand orders. Also verify eager failures beyond the shorter list's end, such as ('a', 'a.²'), and against an absent prerelease, such as ('²', None). No exact exception message is required.

9. Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease='²') < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease='²') is True without error. Independently verify that differing minor and patch components likewise decide ordering without examining these prereleases.

10. Run long-ASCII regression checks on a CPython interpreter with an active decimal integer-string limit below 5000 digits, such as the default 4300. The implementation must neither disable nor alter that limit. Review the changed comparison path to verify ASCII numeric values use normalized length and string comparison rather than integer conversion.

11. The existing pytest suite passes unchanged, including operand handling, subclass, parsing, optional-backend, and comparison regressions. Implementation changes are confined to prerelease comparison logic in src/semver/version.py.
out_of_scope: Writing implementation code during this specification stage.
Changing files other than src/semver/version.py, including tests, docs, changelogs, metadata, dependencies, and packaging.
Changing parsing, validation regexes, or the optional native parser integration.
Changing constructor normalization, stored prerelease text, public signatures, or operand coercion.
Removing legacy Unicode-digit conversion errors or extending the long-ASCII guarantee to non-ASCII digit identifiers.
Changing integer-string conversion settings, core-number handling, bumping, hashing, compatibility checks, or unrelated version behavior.

sealed_tests.notes: Covers long ASCII comparison under an active 4300 digit limit, Unicode compatibility and eager errors, precedence, coercion, operators, parsing, and unchanged public APIs.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.
